rv.q: John R Wilkinson’s absorbing production thrives on simplicity and space, allowing the storytelling and subtle shifts in lighting and sound to transport our imaginations – as well as leaving the gaps that expose where imagination and empathy fall short.
This feels like theatre at its most fundamental: just a man standing in front of us telling us a story, and yet it is also a profound act of engaging your empathy.
Its concept is inventive, the performance of it compelling, and its intentions admirable.

cn.t: Critics praise this inventive Holocaust drama told through an emotional support dog's perspective, calling it moving and compassionate. The clever concept earns acclaim for handling difficult material with delicacy and care.
